messages.author: c9541177104aea27
messages.subject: read lzo compressed files
parts:
Hi all,

We are starting to implement LZO compression for our Hadoop cluster
and now all of our files will be compressed. Is there a way to read
these files with Rhipe ? I have been looking at utilizing jarfiles to
pull in the lzo library, but haven't seen any good examples of
utilizing that feature, plus don't know if it is the way to read the
files.

Thanks,

Jim

messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: read lzo compressed files
parts:

That would be the way, but a little more is required, probably a single class file that converts the Text objects
into RHText objects.

Do you have

a) a JAr to convert text to LZO outpuformat?
b) some LZO libraries for Hadoop?

If you could send this way, i might provide some example of how to do this (i recently wrote one for HBase and one for reading HadoopSequenceFIles that had Text Values and Text Keys)

messages.author: c9541177104aea27
messages.subject: Re: read lzo compressed files
parts:
Hi all,

Sorry, been a couple of weeks, but was able to re-focus on this. Turns 
out much simplier (yet difficult) to get working. But, at this point, I'm 
utilizing rhipe w/ lzo compressed files stored in HDFS. No changes are
needed to my rhipe syntax to read either lzo compress files, or regular
text uncompressed files. 

The key is to have hadoop do all the work, which is where the difficult
piece comes in. Once I installed the hadoop lzo classes and configured
the hadoop environment to handled lzo compressed files (the hard part), 
which included testing with Java, then rhipe falls in for the ride, no changes 
needed, as hadoop does all the work.

Also, as an editorial comment, this is great, as R/rhipe are turning out to be
a great combination for doing analytics on terabytes of data.

Jim
